evals.name: catches-security-and-false-claims-over-nits
evals.prompt: review ~/.claude/skills/deploy-helper before I push it to the team repo
evals.expected_output: A report that ranks any credential leak, disabled TLS verification or unquoted shell variable above naming and formatting findings, with file:line and the offending text quoted for each. A skill-review.json sidecar written beside the skill. Findings the script already reported are carried through, not re-derived.
expectations: Every security finding appears above every convention finding in the report.
Each finding cites a path and line number and quotes the triggering text.
skill-review.json exists and every entry has id, category, finding_type, severity, deterministic, location, evidence and fix.
Every finding_type is one the rubric defines, or the finding sits under out_of_rubric.
anti_expectations: Reports naming, formatting or line-count findings above the credential leak, the disabled TLS verification or the unquoted shell variable
Re-derives a finding scripts/check.py already reported instead of carrying it through
Invents a finding_type the rubric does not define without filing it under out_of_rubric
Emits a finding with no file:line location or no quoted evidence

evals.name: diagnoses-under-triggering-as-a-description-problem
evals.prompt: my changelog skill never fires unless I name it explicitly. what's wrong with it?
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis centred on the description: whether it states when to use the skill, leads with a verb, is written in third person, and contains the concrete words a user would actually type. A proposed replacement description. Body-level findings are reported but not offered as the cause of under-triggering.
expectations: The report names the description field as the trigger mechanism and evaluates it against D1-D9.
A rewritten description is supplied verbatim, not described in the abstract.
The proposed description uses no first or second person and includes explicit trigger conditions.
anti_expectations: Blames body-level findings such as line count or missing references for the under-triggering
Describes how the description should change without supplying the replacement text verbatim
Proposes a replacement written in first or second person, or one that never says when to use the skill

evals.name: runs-the-script-before-the-judgment-pass
evals.prompt: audit every skill under .claude/skills in this repo and tell me which ones I can't ship
evals.expected_output: check.py run once per skill directory, its output used as the deterministic findings. A per-skill verdict driven by blocker count. Mechanical checks such as line counts and frontmatter limits are not re-derived by hand.
expectations: scripts/check.py is executed for each directory containing a SKILL.md.
A skill is called unshippable when and only when it has at least one blocker.
The transcript shows no manual line counting or character counting for checks the script reports.
anti_expectations: Counts lines, characters or frontmatter limits by hand for checks scripts/check.py already reports
Skips scripts/check.py for any directory containing a SKILL.md
Calls a skill shippable while it still has a blocker, or unshippable with none
